text:
A third of Americans between 18 and 34 now live in a parent's home, 24.8 million young adults in all, per new Census data. In New Jersey it's nearly half, and in Connecticut and California it's more than 4 in 10.

These are some of the most expensive places in the country to rent, so I don't blame anyone for moving back home.
why_now: ACS 2025 1-year; holiday weekend, lots of adult kids home.

text: After inflation, the typical rank-and-file worker in America earns $32.75 an hour, about 3% more than the $31.85 they earned in January 1973. The economy has grown enormously since then, but very little of it showed up in the average production worker's paycheck.
why_now: Evergreen labor chart; Oct CPI and earnings data.

text:
Black children who grew up in low-income families were three times as likely as white children from the same income level to be in prison or jail as young adults, according to the Opportunity Atlas.

Even with the same family income and the same starting point, these kids face a very different set of odds.
why_now: Opportunity Atlas; follows the Nov 28 race-gap note with a different outcome.

text:
The US spends $12,099 per person on health care, more than double what Japan spends, and Americans live five fewer years.

Every other rich country on this chart gets more years of life for less money.
why_now: ACA open enrollment; OWID 2023 health spending data.
source_kind: new chart: Our World in Data

text:
In New York, 31% of households don't own a car, and in DC it's 38%. In Wyoming it's under 4%.

Across most of America, not having a car means not being able to get to work, the doctor or a grocery store, so even families who can barely afford one end up paying for one.
why_now: ACS 2025; pairs with the transit reshare this evening.

text:
The average East Flatbush resident lives 0.8 miles from the nearest rail line. Great map from @[Aziz Sunderji](2432780).

The planned Utica Avenue stop on the IBX would put most of them within a half-mile walk of a train, which would make getting to work a lot easier for the people who live there.
why_now: Reshare: Aziz Sunderji ProMap note (Nov 17) on transit access.
source_kind: reshare: Aziz Sunderji / The Pro Map

text:
The top 1% of Americans take home 20.7% of all pre-tax income, about double their share in 1980.

France, Canada and Spain made different policy choices, and the top 1% there takes home around 12%.
why_now: World Inequality Database via OWID; wealth-tax debate continues.
source_kind: new chart: Our World in Data

text:
Only 10% of DC households headed by someone under 35 own their home. In California it's 22.5%, while in West Virginia it's 48.6%.

Many of the places with the most jobs for young people are also the places where buying a first home feels out of reach.

Rents in Austin are down almost 10% since 2022, while rents in the typical large county rose 10%.

Austin built apartments faster than almost any city in America over the past few years, and renters there are now paying less than they did in 2022.

In the US, 5.5 of every 1,000 babies die before their first birthday. In Japan it's 1.8.

The richest country in the world has a higher infant mortality rate than every peer on this chart.
source_kind: new chart: Our World in Data

text:
Nearly 1 in 5 workers in New York spends an hour or more getting to work each way. In Nebraska and South Dakota it's under 4%.

A lot of those long commutes belong to workers who were priced out of the neighborhoods where the jobs are.

There are now 20 counties in America where the typical home is worth more than $1 million, up from 8 in 2019, per Zillow.

In most of them, the people who teach, nurse and police the community can't afford to live there.

Unemployment for Americans aged 16 to 24 is 9.3%, more than double the overall rate of 4.1%.

The November jobs report comes out this morning, and young workers are usually the first to feel a slowdown.

Unemployment ranges from 2% in South Dakota to 5.6% in DC, with California, Connecticut, Michigan and Oregon all at 5% or more.

Today's national number is a single figure, but the job market a family faces depends a lot on where they live.
why_now: Jobs report day; BLS state data (Sept 2026).

text:
The typical household in DC earns $109,505 a year. In Mississippi it's $59,346, per new Census data.

Families in DC have almost twice as much to work with before rent, groceries or child care.

More than 1 in 5 working-age adults in Texas has no health insurance. In Massachusetts it's fewer than 1 in 25.

Massachusetts built near-universal coverage two decades ago, and Texas is one of the few states that still hasn't expanded Medicaid.
why_now: ACS 2025; ACA deadline for Jan 1 coverage is Dec 15.

text: American workers put in about 1,789 hours a year on average, roughly 450 more than workers in Germany. Over a year, the difference adds up to about 11 extra weeks of full-time work.
source_kind: new chart: Our World in Data

text:
Which state has the highest share of households with no internet access at all?

The answer is West Virginia, at 7.8%, nearly twice the national rate. Most of the states near the top of this list are rural and lower-income, and getting families online there would open up a lot of opportunity.

text:
In DC, 18.4% of residents 60 and older live below the poverty line. In Louisiana it's 16.1%.

Many of these are people who worked their whole lives. In much of the country, a Social Security check alone doesn't cover rent and medicine.

22.7% of workers in DC now work from home, compared with 6.3% in North Dakota and 6.5% in Mississippi.

Remote work became a perk of higher-income jobs, while most service workers never got the option.

Home values fell over the past year in 23% of US counties, per Zillow.

For most families the house is the bulk of their wealth, so a falling home value means a thinner safety net, even when the national numbers look fine.
why_now: Zillow ZHVI Oct 2026; follows the K-shaped home values reshare.
